# zdotu

> Forms the dot product of two complex vectors ZDOTU = Xᵀ·Y.

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```js
import zdotu from '@rreusser/blahpack/blas/base/zdotu';
```

### Layout API

Takes a storage layout (`order`) and leading dimensions, like CBLAS/LAPACKE.

```js
zdotu( N, x, strideX, y, strideY ) → Complex128
```

| param | type | intent | shape | constraints | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | number of elements in input vector(s) |
| `x` | `Complex128Array` | in | `N` |  | storage spacing between elements of ZX. |
| ↳ `strideX` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride length for `x` |
| `y` | `Complex128Array` | in | `N` |  | storage spacing between elements of ZY. |
| ↳ `strideY` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride length for `y` |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `N`: number of elements in input vector(s)

</details>

**Returns** `Complex128`: unconjugated dot product

### Strided (ndarray) API

Takes explicit strides and offsets for every array. Use it for views, sub-matrices and non-unit strides.

```js
zdotu.ndarray( N, x, strideX, offsetX, y, strideY, offsetY ) → Complex128
```

Forms the dot product of two complex vectors ZDOTU = Xᵀ·Y, using alternative indexing semantics.

| param | type | intent | shape | constraints | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | number of complex elements |
| `x` | `Complex128Array` | in | `N` |  | first complex input vector |
| ↳ `strideX` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride for `x` (in complex elements) |
| ↳ `offsetX` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | starting index for `x` (in complex elements) |
| `y` | `Complex128Array` | in | `N` |  | second complex input vector |
| ↳ `strideY` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride for `y` (in complex elements) |
| ↳ `offsetY` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | starting index for `y` (in complex elements) |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `N`: number of elements in input vector(s)

</details>

**Returns** `Complex128`: unconjugated dot product

</section>

<!-- /.usage -->

<section class="notes">

## Notes

-   `zdotu()` corresponds to the reference BLAS routine [`ZDOTU`](https://github.com/Reference-LAPACK/lapack/blob/v3.12.0/BLAS/SRC/zdotu.f).

</section>

<!-- /.notes -->

<section class="examples">

## Examples

```js
import Complex128Array from '@stdlib/array/complex128/lib/index.js';
import zdotu from '@rreusser/blahpack/blas/base/zdotu';

// Compute unconjugated dot product of complex vectors:
const x = new Complex128Array( [ 1.0, 0.0, 0.0, 1.0 ] );
const y = new Complex128Array( [ 1.0, 0.0, 0.0, 1.0 ] );

// Using the standard interface:
let result = zdotu( 2, x, 1, y, 1 );
console.log( result ); // eslint-disable-line no-console

// Using the ndarray interface:
result = zdotu.ndarray( 2, x, 1, 0, y, 1, 0 );
console.log( result ); // eslint-disable-line no-console
```

</section>

<!-- /.examples -->

<section class="reference-notes">

## Reference notes

The mathematical description from the reference BLAS 3.12.0 source of `ZDOTU`. Indices are the 1-based Fortran indices of the source.

### Purpose

ZDOTU forms the dot product of two complex vectors

$$
\mathrm{ZDOTU} = X^T \, Y
$$

### Further Details

jack dongarra, 3/11/78. modified 12/3/93, array(1) declarations changed to array(\*)

</section>
